data.title: Akamai Signs $11.6 Billion Anthropic Cloud Deal, Plans $5.5 Billion in Capex
data.description:
Akamai Technologies (NASDAQ: AKAM) has signed an expanded seven-year cloud services commitment with Anthropic worth approximately $11.6 billion. The agreement adds a large, long-dated customer contract to Akamai’s AI infrastructure business, while requiring substantial investment before the full revenue run rate arrives.

Akamai said the plans cover dedicated cloud computing capacity and related services to support Anthropic’s growing CPU workloads. The companies entered the plans on September 18 under an existing master services agreement; Akamai announced them on September 24. Anthropic’s payments are subject to contract termination provisions and Akamai meeting delivery and service-availability requirements, according to the company’s SEC filing. Reuters separately reported the seven-year commitment.

The timing matters. Akamai’s investor presentation estimates service will begin late in the second quarter of 2027, with $150 million to $300 million in contract revenue during fiscal 2027. The company projects the revenue to ramp through 2028 and reach an annualized rate of about $1.7 billion by year-end. Those are management estimates, not current sales. Akamai’s deal presentation also puts related capital spending at about $5.5 billion over the buildout, including an additional $1.7 billion in 2026. The company said the agreement does not change its 2026 revenue guidance.

The contract could expand by as much as another $9 billion, bringing the potential total to roughly $20 billion, but that additional business is conditional. Akamai also issued Anthropic a warrant that could represent up to about 5% of Akamai’s common shares on conversion. The SEC filing says vesting depends on payment and additional commercial commitments, so the full amount is not immediate or assured.

The agreement gives investors a concrete measure of demand for Akamai’s distributed compute capacity, but it also ties the opportunity to a multiyear construction and service ramp. The key milestones will be whether capacity is delivered on schedule, the customer commitments convert into recognized revenue, and the added spending produces the returns Akamai projects. The company’s announcement describes the relationship as an expansion of its cloud platform for AI workloads.

data.title: U.S.-China Trade Truce Extended to Jan. 10, Bessent Says
data.description:
The United States and China will extend their trade truce through Jan. 10, 2027, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday, Sept. 23. His announcement moves the existing Nov. 10 deadline back by two months, just before Chinese President Xi Jinping’s state visit with President Donald Trump in Washington. Bessent made the announcement in a Fox News interview after meeting Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng. The White House had scheduled Xi’s state visit for Thursday, Sept. 24.

Bessent called the arrangement the Busan agreement and said the extra time would let both governments continue working on economic issues. Reuters reported that the 2025 truce paused an escalating tariff fight in which duties between the two countries had topped 100%. The latest announcement extends the timetable; it does not spell out a new tariff schedule or a broader trade package.

For companies that make, source or sell products across the two markets, the extension delays the next major decision point around existing tariff arrangements. That gives businesses more time to plan under the current framework, but it does not settle what happens after January or remove other sources of trade uncertainty. The Bessent announcement named no company-specific exemptions or commitments.

A Bloomberg report carried by Yahoo Finance said Bessent described the talks as unfinished and did not know whether the countries could reach a larger deal. The extension is therefore a short-term continuation of the current arrangement, not evidence of a lasting settlement. Disputes involving technology controls, critical minerals and market access remain potential points of friction, Reuters reported.

Reuters also reported that the summit could produce discussions or announcements on agriculture and other trade barriers, but those were not part of the extension announced by Bessent. For investors, the two-month reprieve shifts the near-term policy calendar without resolving the longer-term outlook for cross-border costs and supply chains.

data.title: NYSE and Blockchain.com Explore 24/7 Access to Tokenized Stocks
data.description:
NYSE Group and Blockchain.com have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore offering tokenized U.S.-listed stocks and exchange-traded funds through the exchange’s planned digital platform. The collaboration could connect traditional market infrastructure with Blockchain.com’s global crypto user base, although the service remains subject to regulatory approvals.

The proposed arrangement would use the NYSE’s digital alternative trading system to provide access to tokenized securities, according to the companies’ announcement. Blockchain.com said its platform has more than 44 million confirmed accounts. The parties also plan to explore exchanging market data, including ICE (NYSE: ICE) and NYSE data for Blockchain.com’s application.

Tokenized stocks represent traditional securities on blockchain infrastructure. If approved and launched, the structure could support fractional ownership, extended-hours access and faster on-chain settlement. Those features remain proposed benefits rather than an operating service available to investors today.

The agreement is strategically important for Intercontinental Exchange, NYSE’s parent, because it gives the exchange a potential distribution channel among crypto-native users. It also places the NYSE alongside financial and digital-asset firms testing whether blockchain rails can expand market access without weakening the rights and protections attached to traditional securities.

The companies have not disclosed financial terms or a launch date, and the eventual list of eligible stocks and ETFs is not yet defined. Regulatory approval and the design of the digital trading system will determine whether the memorandum becomes a commercial product. For now, the announcement is an infrastructure and market-access initiative, not a completed change to how NYSE-listed shares trade.

data.title: What’s Ahead for the Stock Market This Week
data.description:
After Friday’s sharp selloff triggered by President Trump’s decision to raise tariffs in response to China tightening rare earth exports, investors are starting the week on edge. The focus now shifts to trade tensions, earnings season, and the Federal Reserve’s next moves.

Big Earnings Week: Banks and Chipmakers Take Center Stage

This week kicks off a busy stretch of third-quarter results from major financial firms and tech companies.

  • Banks: JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Citigroup all report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Later in the week, American Express, Truist Financial, and State Street will wrap up the financial lineup.
  • Tech & Chips: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) reports Thursday after strong AI chip sales boosted its revenue 40% in the first half of 2025. ASML follows on Wednesday after raising concerns about tariffs and slowing demand for chip equipment.
  • Tech events: Oracle’s AI World conference begins Monday, and Salesforce’s Dreamforce starts Tuesday — both likely to bring attention to artificial intelligence and enterprise tech. Earnings Calendar >>

Data Delays and Fed Watch

The federal government shutdown, now entering its third week, is likely to delay several key reports, including retail sales, inflation (PPI), housing starts, and jobless claims. Some data will still come through, like the NFIB Small Business Optimism Index on Tuesday and homebuilder confidence on Thursday.

Investors will also tune in to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s speech on Tuesday, along with comments from Fed officials, including Michelle Bowman and Christopher Waller. The Fed’s Beige Book, which gives an overview of economic conditions across regions, will be released on Wednesday.

Market Context

Bond markets will be closed on Monday for Columbus Day (also observed as Indigenous Peoples Day), but stock exchanges will remain open.

With limited economic data and uncertainty around Washington’s budget standoff, markets are likely to take their cues from corporate earnings and Fed commentary.

In short, this week is about navigating through noise — balancing worries over tariffs and the shutdown against potential optimism from strong bank and chipmaker earnings.

data.title: What Is the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA)? A Complete Guide
data.description:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA), often referred to as the Dow Jones, the Dow 30, or simply the Dow, is one of the world’s most recognized stock market indexes. The DJIA tracks 30 of the largest publicly traded companies in the United States, making it a widely followed indicator of the overall health of the U.S. economy and stock market. Investors searching for DJIA today, DJIA futures, or Dow Jones price updates often turn to this index as a barometer of market sentiment.

But what exactly is the DJIA, what stocks does it include, and how do traders and long-term investors use it in their strategies?

What Is the DJIA?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) is a price-weighted index created in 1896 by Charles Dow and Edward Jones. Unlike market-cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500, the DJIA assigns weight based on a stock’s price rather than its market capitalization. This means a company with a higher stock price (e.g., Apple or UnitedHealth) influences the index more heavily than lower-priced stocks.

The DJIA is designed to reflect the performance of blue-chip companies across different sectors of the U.S. economy. It does not include utilities or transportation stocks, which are tracked by separate Dow indexes.

What Companies Are in the DJIA?

The DJIA is composed of 30 large, publicly traded U.S. companies that are considered leaders in their industries. These companies span sectors such as technology, finance, healthcare, consumer goods, and industrials.

Here’s a snapshot of the DJIA holdings (as of 2025, September 15th):

Note: The index is reviewed periodically, and constituents may change depending on mergers, bankruptcies, or shifts in market relevance.

How Does the DJIA Work?

  • Price-Weighted Methodology: Higher-priced stocks have more influence.
  • Dow Divisor: A proprietary number adjusted for stock splits, dividends, and corporate actions ensures continuity.
  • Sector Balance: While tech stocks (Apple, Microsoft) now hold significant weight, the index aims to represent the broader U.S. economy.

If Apple (AAPL) rises $5 in a day, it has the same impact on the DJIA as Boeing (BA) rising $5, even though their market caps differ drastically.

Why Do Investors Watch the DJIA?

  • Economic Barometer: The DJIA today is seen as a snapshot of the U.S. economy.
  • Historical Importance: Created in 1896, it has over 125 years of market history.
  • Market Sentiment: Widely quoted on news outlets and financial platforms.
  • Trading Opportunities: Investors follow DJIA futures, DJIA ETFs, and Dow Jones index funds for exposure.

How to Trade or Invest in the DJIA

Investors can’t buy the DJIA directly but can gain exposure through exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures contracts, or mutual funds:

  • SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) – tracks the DJIA closely.
  • DJIA Futures – contracts traded on CME, allowing leveraged exposure.
  • Index Funds – designed for long-term buy-and-hold investors.

data.title: UK Banks Complete First Live Customer Transactions With Tokenized Deposits
data.description:
Several major UK banks have completed live customer transactions using tokenized sterling deposits, giving commercial-bank money a practical test on shared blockchain infrastructure. UK Finance said on September 24 that the pilot included two remortgage completions and a consumer marketplace transaction.

The Great British Tokenised Deposit initiative involved Barclays, HSBC UK, Lloyds Banking Group (NYSE: LYG), Monzo, Nationwide, NatWest and Santander. In the mortgage tests, funds were locked and automatically released at completion. The project also tested a payment moving between institutions for a simulated online purchase, according to UK Finance.

Tokenized deposits are digital representations of ordinary commercial-bank deposits. They are designed to preserve the banking relationship and regulatory protections of traditional money while adding programmable features, such as conditional settlement and automated release of funds.

The development matters to listed banks because faster settlement and shared infrastructure could eventually reduce manual processing in areas such as property transactions and cross-bank payments. It is still an industry pilot, however, and does not establish a commercial revenue stream or prove that tokenized deposits will replace existing payment rails.

UK Finance said the project is also exploring person-to-person payments and future digital-asset settlement. The next stage will be determining whether the technology can operate at scale while meeting operational, privacy, consumer-protection and regulatory requirements. For investors, the announcement is best viewed as an infrastructure milestone rather than a near-term earnings catalyst.

data.title: Royal Caribbean Takes 50% Sandals Stake in Push Beyond Cruises
data.description:
Royal Caribbean Group (NYSE: RCL) is expanding beyond cruise ships through a planned 50% investment in Sandals and Beaches Resorts. The companies announced the partnership on September 23, saying Royal Caribbean will invest approximately $3 billion in cash to support the all-inclusive resort operator’s growth.

The agreement gives Royal Caribbean exposure to a different part of the leisure market while keeping Sandals and Beaches under a joint-venture structure. The partners said the arrangement is intended to broaden Royal Caribbean’s vacation platform and create opportunities for additional resort development across the Caribbean, according to the company announcement.

For Royal Caribbean, the deal adds land-based stays that can complement its cruise itineraries and gives the company another way to participate in customers’ travel spending. It also increases exposure to resort economics, including construction costs, staffing, occupancy and regional tourism demand.

The transaction is a strategic expansion rather than an immediate earnings update. The companies did not provide a detailed forecast for revenue, profit or returns from the partnership in the announcement. Investors will therefore need to assess how the $3 billion investment is funded, when the transaction closes and how quickly new resort capacity can contribute.

The move comes as travel companies continue to broaden their offerings around the full vacation journey. Royal Caribbean’s existing cruise brands and Sandals’ all-inclusive resorts serve overlapping leisure customers, but the businesses have different operating models. The partnership’s eventual value will depend on whether the combined platform can generate incremental bookings without adding disproportionate operating or capital costs.

data.title: Meta Expands AI Glasses Lineup as Muse Moves Beyond the Phone
data.description:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) is extending its consumer-AI push from the phone to the face. At its Connect event on September 23, the company introduced Ray-Ban Meta Audio, expanded its AI-glasses lineup and said its Muse personal agent will work through the glasses.

Meta said Muse will let users manage tasks hands-free through its AI glasses, while the expanded portfolio will include products across Ray-Ban, Oakley and Meta Glasses. The company said it expects to offer more than 100 AI-glasses options by the end of 2026, according to its official Connect announcement.

The announcement adds a hardware distribution channel to Muse, which Meta launched earlier this month as a personal agent designed to act across a user’s connected apps. Meta’s product description says Muse can help with tasks such as email, travel planning and shopping, subject to user permissions and safety checks.

For investors, the significance is less about one new glasses model than about the potential relationship between hardware adoption and recurring AI use. Glasses can make the assistant available during commutes, errands and other moments when reaching for a phone is inconvenient. That could give Meta more opportunities to build daily engagement around its AI products, although the company has not disclosed a financial forecast tied specifically to Muse or the new glasses.

Meta is also adding competition to a wearable-AI market that includes devices from technology and consumer-electronics companies. The rollout will test whether consumers view camera, audio and assistant features as useful enough to justify wearing connected glasses regularly. Meta’s announcement says some new capabilities, including Muse access, are planned for the glasses ecosystem, so adoption and execution remain important next steps rather than established revenue outcomes.

data.title: Stocks Slide as Oil Surge and Stronger Business Activity Lift Rate Concerns
data.description:
U.S. stocks retreated on Wednesday, September 23, as a sharp rise in oil prices and stronger-than-expected private-sector activity pushed Treasury yields higher and revived concerns that the Federal Reserve may need to keep interest rates elevated. The move pulled the major indexes away from recent highs and weighed especially on large technology companies.

The S&P 500 fell 0.74% to 7,706.39, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.10% to 26,943.61, according to Reuters reporting carried by Fidelity. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and other semiconductor shares were among the technology names under pressure. Alphabet and Amazon also dragged on the session, Reuters reported.

Brent crude rose almost 4% after renewed tension involving Iran, with the benchmark settling near $103 a barrel, according to Reuters. Higher energy prices matter for stocks because they can add to headline inflation and reduce the room for rate cuts. They also raise operating costs for transportation, airlines and other fuel-sensitive industries.

At the same time, a business survey showed U.S. manufacturing and services activity accelerating in September at the fastest pace in more than five years, according to Yahoo Finance's market report. Stronger activity is positive for growth, but in this market it also reinforced the view that demand may keep inflation above the Federal Reserve's 2% goal.

The backdrop is unusually sensitive to incoming data. The Federal Open Market Committee raised its target range by a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16 and said inflation remained elevated in its latest statement. Wednesday's combination of firmer activity, higher oil and rising yields therefore challenged the market's expectation that policy could soon become less restrictive. It does not establish that another increase is certain, but it raises the importance of the next inflation and labor-market readings.

data.title: Netflix Stock Slides After Wells Fargo Downgrade Flags Engagement Concerns
data.description:
Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) shares fell nearly 5% on Friday after Wells Fargo downgraded the streaming company to Underweight from Equal Weight and cut its price target to $57 from $80. The move made Netflix one of the day's notable decliners as investors weighed whether its content strategy is keeping viewers engaged.

Wells Fargo analyst Steven Cahall said engagement trends looked worrying, according to reporting carried by Yahoo Finance. The note cited an 8% decline in viewing time per subscriber per day in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2023. The brokerage also argued that Netflix has lacked a consistent run of major original series and may need to rethink its content spending.

The downgrade comes as Netflix expands beyond its traditional streaming offer into areas including games and podcasts. Wells Fargo's concern is not that those initiatives cannot add value, but that they could draw attention and resources away from the original programming that drives the platform's strongest viewing spikes.

Netflix's stock has already lost roughly one-quarter of its value this year, according to Yahoo Finance. The reaction to Friday's note therefore extends an existing market debate rather than creating a new company filing or operating update. Netflix has not announced a change to its full-year outlook in connection with the downgrade.

For investors, the key question is whether the engagement data reflects a temporary gap between hit releases or a more durable shift in the economics of streaming content. The answer will depend on Netflix's next slate of releases, subscriber trends and management's explanation of how new formats support the core service. Friday's decline shows that analysts are demanding clearer evidence that expansion will reinforce, rather than dilute, Netflix's central content engine.

Yahoo Finance reported on the downgrade and the market reaction, while Netflix's investor-relations site provides the company's official filings and disclosures.
